description.short: BikePark Wales at Gethin Woodland, Merthyr Tydfil, is the UK's biggest and most diverse mountain bike park. Set on a 491 m summit within NRW-managed Gethin Forest, it offers 47+ purpose-built descents from green beginner runs to expert pro-lines, a minibus uplift service, bike hire, coaching, and a full visitor hub — all just 1 mile off the A470.
description.shortNote: Drafted from verified sources. Trail count varies across sources (47, 50+, 60+) — use 47 as the internal-CSV figure and note 'over 47' to hedge; editorial team should verify exact current count from bikeparkwales.com.
description.full:
BikePark Wales is a private commercial mountain bike park operating within Gethin Forest, a Natural Resources Wales-managed woodland on the hills above Merthyr Tydfil, South Wales. The park operates under a 33-year lease with NRW (signed 2024) and has been recognised jointly with NRW for its Future Forest Vision, balancing recreation, biodiversity, and sustainable forestry.

Set at an elevation of up to 491 m (Mynydd Gethin summit), the park offers over 47 purpose-built descents graded green, blue, red, black, and orange/pro. Kermit — a 4.2 km green descent — is widely described as the UK's longest beginner downhill trail. Other named trails include Terry's Belly (blue), Dai Hard (red), Vicious Valley (red), A470 (black), and the pro-line 50 to 01 (orange). A 4.6 km pedal-up singletrack climb and pedal passes provide alternatives to the uplift service.

The visitor hub at Gethin Woodland Centre includes The Woodland Café (breakfasts, burgers, refreshments), a bike shop, workshop, bike and equipment hire (Trek bikes), professional coaching, uplift minibuses (bookable up to 3 months in advance), free parking, toilets, showers, changing facilities, and Wi-Fi. The park accommodates individuals, families, groups, schools, and corporate events, and offers annual memberships. It has Visit Wales Quality Assured status.
